title: Upgrade Micetro from 26.1 to 26.2

cta.text: See what is new in Micetro 26.2

prompt:
Product: BlueCat. Demo: "Upgrade Micetro from 26.1 to 26.2".
Start with one welcome step whose title is exactly "Upgrade Micetro in Two Deliberate Steps" and whose text is exactly: A new Micetro release is out. Watch the administrator check for it, read what changed, stage it on every server, deploy it, and sign back in on 26.2 with the Microsoft estate exactly as it was.
Audience: network and DNS engineers and IT leaders evaluating the product. Tone: concise, confident, practical, no hype.
9 screenshots, keep this order, one tooltip per image, calling out the highlighted UI element. Use the text of each numbered tooltip EXACTLY as written; do not rewrite, shorten or merge it. Do not add a closing step or a closing message after the last screenshot; its own tooltip is the end.
1. Micetro tells the administrator when a new version is ready. A notice like this one appears in the Admin page. Select it to see what is on offer.
2. Micetro 26.2.0 is offered, with every component it will update: Central, the DNS and DHCP agents, the appliance and the web application. Only the administrator user can run it.
3. Read what is in the release before you commit to it. Nothing has been installed yet.
4. Prepare update downloads the package and stages it on every server. Nothing is live yet, so this can happen any time before your change window.
5. When you are ready, Deploy update asks for confirmation first, because Micetro is unavailable while it runs.
6. Confirm, and Micetro shows it is being updated to 26.2.0 while Central restarts.
7. A short restart later, the console reports 26.2.0 and says you are running the latest version.
8. Every component is on 26.2.0 and up to date, including the agents on the DNS and DHCP servers, which were updated for you.
9. Same servers, same scopes, same zones. The upgrade touched Micetro, not the estate it manages.
